verdicts.argument: The wording is real. 10-K FY2025 p.27 adds the 'insufficient to offset pricing concessions' clause, which does not appear in 10-K FY2024 p.26. 10-Q 2026Q2 p.25 gives the Bridge Program dates as July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027 and says 'The uptake from this expanded access is unknown.' The arithmetic is also right: -10% x $30,375M = $3,038M, and -5% x $19,304M (H1 2025 U.S., 10-Q p.28) = $965M. The problem is that the math touches the wrong price give-up. The 2025 U.S. price decline of 10% (10-K p.49) is attributed to Mounjaro and Zepbound generally. Most of 2025 came before the November 2025 preliminary agreement, and the Bridge only started July 1, 2026, after the 10-Q period ends. The H1 2026 -5% includes the 'previously announced reductions in cash-pay prices' (10-Q p.29). Q2 U.S. price was only -3% because a favorable rebate true-up worth 3% of U.S. revenue (10-Q p.10, p.28) offset it. So '~$1B per half-year price give-up' cannot be read as the deal's concession that the volume must offset.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to the disclosure change: a new 10-K clause admitting deal revenue may not offset concessions, plus a 10-Q end date for Medicare access. Do not size it with total U.S. price erosion. Most of the 2025 -10% predates the deal, and the Bridge's concession and volume both begin only in Q3 2026, so the deal's price cost is not yet visible in any filed period.

verdicts.argument: The claimed flip did not happen. 10-K FY2024 p.32 already says the risk 'may render built or in process manufacturing capacity unnecessary, and may also subject us to contractual payment obligations, which may be significant.' The same FY2024 paragraph also already says 'tirzepatide supply currently exceeds demand in the U.S.' The only FY2025 change (10-K p.34) is that 'overestimation of demand or' was inserted before 'events that limit demand.' That is a three-word edit, not a new warning. The PP&E figures check: 24,675/17,102 = +44.3% (10-K p.59), and 29,286/24,675 = +18.7% (10-Q p.7). The impairment sizing is a made-up 10% haircut, and its arithmetic is slightly off: 10% x $12,184M = $1,218M; x (1 - 0.199) = $976M; / 893.7M shares = $1.09/share, not $1.07.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: FY2025 added 'overestimation of demand' to an existing overcapacity risk that already mentioned stranded capacity and significant contractual payments. No disclosed impairment or charge. PP&E +44% is a fact but not evidence of overbuild.

verdicts.argument: All operands match. Revenue 65,179/45,043 = +44.7% and COGS 11,052/8,418 (10-K p.57). Accounts receivable 17,760/11,006 = +61.4% and inventories 13,744/7,589 = +81.1% (10-K p.59). These are current inventories, and they tie to Note 6 total 13,701 + LIFO 43 (p.70). WIP 8,183/3,979 = +105.7%. DIO is 453.9 vs 329.1 days, and the $1.5B pre-launch inventory is confirmed on p.70. A better comparator for year-end receivables is Q4 revenue: Q4 2025 = 65,179 - 45,887 (10-Q 2025Q3 p.5) = 19,292 vs Q4 2024 13,533, or +42.6%. Receivables still outran it. Two issues are left out. First, the receivables gap reversed by mid-2026: AR 20,083 (10-Q 2026Q2 p.7) vs 14,170.4 (10-Q 2025Q2 p.7) = +41.7%, against Q2 revenue +47.7% (10-Q p.5). Second, pre-launch stock has no COGS yet. Excluding it, DIO is (13,744 - 1,500)/11,052 x 365 = 404 days, still up from 329. The write-off EPS math (1,500 x 0.801 / 893.7 = $1.34) uses a consistent share count.
verdicts.correction: The 2025 inventory build holds, including excluding pre-launch stock (DIO 404 vs 329). The receivables leg is a 2025 fact only: by 6/30/2026 receivables (+41.7% YoY) grew slower than revenue (+47.7%), so do not present receivables as an ongoing divergence.

verdicts.argument: The 2025 roll-forward leg holds. Deductions 62,135 vs 41,452 = +49.9% (10-K FY2025 p.54) against U.S. revenue 43,481 vs 30,375 = +43.1% (p.49). Implied gross-to-net (GTN) went from 63.5% (2023) to 57.7% (2024) to 58.8% (2025). Holding 2024's GTN on 2025 gross of $105.6B would have given about $1.18B more revenue, or 1.8% of revenue, which is material. The mid-2026 liability leg mixes lines. The balance-sheet 'Sales rebates and discounts' of 21,122 vs 14,537.4 (+45.3%; 10-Q 2026Q2 p.7, 10-Q 2025Q2 p.7) is consolidated. 10-K p.54 says 13% of it was ex-U.S. at YE2025, up from 10%. Against the matching consolidated base, Q2 revenue rose 47.7% (22,974 vs 15,558, 10-Q p.5), so the liability grew slower than sales, not faster. Comparing it with U.S. Q2 revenue (+33%) is the wrong denominator, and ex-U.S. revenue grew 80%. The true-up math checks: 3% x 14,413 = $432M, and Q2 tax 2,152/9,247 = 23.3% (p.15), so $432M x 0.767 / 893.7 = $0.37. But 'non-recurring' is shaky: the same adjustment was 3% of U.S. revenue for all of 2024 (10-K p.64), so it recurs in some years.
verdicts.correction: Keep the 2025 GTN re-widening (57.7% to 58.8%, about $1.2B). Drop 'liability outrunning U.S. sales into mid-2026': the consolidated liability (+45%) trailed consolidated revenue (+48%). State the Q2 2026 true-up as a $432M (~$0.37) favorable item, the largest quarterly rate since FY2024's 3%.

verdicts.argument: The ten-product drop is real. The FY2025 Note 2 table (p.65) no longer lists Humalog, Humulin, Basaglar, Baqsimi, Cyramza, Erbitux, Tyvyt, Olumiant, Emgality or Zyprexa, all of which appear on 10-K FY2024 p.68. The MD&A table went from 16 named products (FY2024 p.49) to 3 (FY2025 p.49). This is a presentation change, not a restatement. The FY2024 lines reconcile: U.S. 1,502.6 + 643.4 + 375.4 + 2.5 + 159.6 = 2,683.5 vs restated 2,682, and ex-U.S. 1,777.2 vs 1,778. The impact math is wrong in two places. First, the '7.5% to 35.2%' comparison mixes two definitions of 'Other products.' The FY2025 10-K itself restates 2024 Other products as $23,270M (p.49). On a like-for-like basis the bucket fell 1.4% (23,270 to 22,949), and its share fell from 51.7% to 35.2% of revenue. Second, the 16.7% U.S. decline is not hidden: 'Other cardiometabolic health 2,233 / 2,682' is printed on p.65. Only the split among insulins is lost. The -$449M is 0.7% of revenue, below the 1% bar. It also follows a 2024 Humalog U.S. jump of +74% (863.2 to 1,502.6, FY2024 p.68), so part of it is reversion.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: the FY2025 10-K aggregated ten previously named products into category lines. This is a presentation change with no restated totals. The legacy insulin bucket's U.S. decline (-16.7%, -$449M, 0.7% of revenue) is still visible on p.65. Drop the 7.5% to 35.2% 'Other products' comparison: like-for-like the bucket fell 1.4%.

verdicts.argument: The figures match. Contingent consideration was 34 + 217 = 251 at YE2025 and 814 + 1,704 = 2,518 at 6/30/2026, or 10.0x (10-Q p.17). Kelonia's maximum is $3,750M against fair value of $1,765M, and Centessa's is $1,542M against $402M (p.13, footnote 3 confirms 'maximum amount of potential payments'). The arithmetic is right: 5,292 - 2,167 = 3,125, and x 0.801 / 893.7 = $2.80. Three materiality caveats apply. (1) The $3.1B is a ceiling that requires every milestone to hit. Milestone success would also raise the value of the acquired IPR&D, so the charge is not an unconditional earnings drag. (2) Fair-value remeasurement of contingent consideration is often not tax-deductible, so applying a 19.9% tax shield may understate the per-share hit. With no shield it is up to $3.50. (3) '$814M now due within a year' overstates it: it is fair value classified as current, not a fixed amount owed. The July 2026 '$3.9B in aggregate' (p.14) is total deal value, not contingent consideration, and should not be added to the remeasurement ceiling.
verdicts.correction: Contingent consideration rose from $251M to $2.5B (mostly Kelonia). The undiscounted maximum exceeds booked fair value by about $3.1B, which is a ceiling on future remeasurement charges that would only arise alongside milestone success. Do not add the July 2026 deal value.

verdicts.argument: The EPS math uses the right base and share count. The rate rose from 16.5% to 19.8% (10-K p.80). That is (0.198 - 0.165) x pretax $25,731M = $849M, divided by FY2025 diluted shares of 899.3M (p.57) = $0.94. Cash taxes of $10,814M vs expense of $5,091M = 2.1x (p.79). Two problems remain. First, 'rose ... to 19.9% in H1 2026' mixes periods: 19.9% is a six-month rate and is flat against FY2025's 19.8%. The like-for-like change is H1 2026 19.9% vs H1 2025 17.7% (10-Q p.15), which is 2.2pp x $18,097M = $398M, or about $0.44/share on 894.8M diluted. Second, the 2.1x cash-to-book ratio is partly one-time: p.79 says the increase was 'driven primarily by a $4.2 billion increase in Ireland resulting from higher production activity ... and a prior year tax payment.' A useful link the reader missed: prepaid taxes went from $7.1B to $12.9B (+82%, p.79), in step with inventory +81%.
verdicts.correction: FY2025 rate step-up = ~$0.94/share (holds). For 2026, cite +2.2pp H1-over-H1 (~$0.44 for the half), not 19.8% to 19.9%. Present the cash-tax gap as an Irish production and inventory timing effect inflated by a prior-year payment, not a recurring 2x.

verdicts.argument: The quotes and the grade-B transcript are confirmed (LLY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p.1). The speakers are confirmed too: Shin asked, Ricks answered, Breen asked, and Custer answered. But the math does not touch what the quotes say. Ricks' 'I don't think that per se that reads through to some pricing effect' answers whether Cigna's switch from rebates to GPO fees changes industry pricing. It is not a statement about Lilly's own GTN trend, so a 1.1pp GTN widening in the later 10-K does not contradict it. Breen asked 'Can you help us understand kind of the potential for expansion to the market with orfo?' Custer's market-size answer was responsive to that question, not a dodge on inventory. The impact numbers ($1.06B per GTN point, $1.5B pre-launch inventory) are copied from c03 and c04 and add nothing new.
verdicts.correction: Fold into c03 and c04. There is no independent contradiction between the call and the filings at material scale.

verdicts.argument: The facts check out. The Zepbound label lists weight management and OSA only (drug:zepbound p.2). Wegovy injection has CV and MASH indications, and the tablets have CV (drug:wegovy p.2). Tirzepatide 'Morbidity and mortality in obesity' is Phase 3 ongoing, and the CV outcomes in T2D is submitted, which is a Mounjaro indication (10-K FY2025 p.44). The Novo slide line is on NVO 2025Q4 slides p.33. The Bridge runs to 12/31/2027 (10-Q p.25). Zepbound U.S. H1 2026 = $9,006M (10-Q p.29), so the $18.0B annualized and $180M per 1% are correct. On materiality, though, nothing is sized. Medicare share is undisclosed, the Bridge only began 7/1/2026 so no Medicare Zepbound volume is in any reported period, and 10-Q p.25 says Lilly 'continue[s] to engage with [CMS] on long-term Medicare access.' A 1% sensitivity ($180M, 0.3% of revenue) is below the bar unless Medicare is a large share.
verdicts.correction: Keep as a label-gap risk dated to 12/31/2027, not a revenue estimate. Say plainly that no reported period yet contains Bridge volume, so the at-risk base is currently zero in reported revenue.

verdicts.argument: Q2 2026 Mounjaro U.S. was $4,791M vs ex-U.S. $5,152M (10-Q p.29, p.10). But the crossover did not happen in Q2. The H1 figures are U.S. 9,024 vs ex-U.S. 9,582 (p.29), so Q1 2026 was already U.S. 4,233 vs ex-U.S. 4,430. The -36% Q2 ex-U.S. price is for all products, not Mounjaro specifically (p.28), though p.28 attributes it mainly to Mounjaro's NRDL listing. Price math: -31% x 8,983 = $2,785M on the correct prior-year base. The exact '75% of Mounjaro revenue outside the U.S. ... paying out of pocket' quote is in the prepared-remarks block the transcript assigns to Lucas Montarce, not Patrik Jonsson. Jonsson separately said '75% out-of-pocket.' Both are on a grade-B transcript, p.1. The IRA share of 9,999/65,179 = 15.3% uses worldwide revenue for a U.S.-Medicare program. U.S.-only it is (2,914 + 3,464)/65,179 = 9.8%. Novo's 79.9% in force_summary.csv is also on a worldwide basis, so the comparison is internally consistent but overstates both companies.
verdicts.correction: Mounjaro ex-U.S. revenue has exceeded U.S. revenue since Q1 2026 (Q1 4,430 vs 4,233; Q2 5,152 vs 4,791). Attribute the exact 75% quote to Montarce. If IRA exposure is mentioned, use 9.8% U.S.-only for Lilly.

verdicts.argument: The five NADAC rows exist verbatim in data/moat/tables/nadac_history.csv at the cited lines. They are machine-generated CMS survey rows with no page in the citation index, so they can be cited as data points but cannot be quoted as filing language. The unit math is right: 7.5 mg KwikPen is 30 mg in 2.4 mL, which is 4 doses, giving $482.20 vs $1,052.01 (-54.2%). At 15 mg it is $675.43 vs $1,051.84 (-35.8%). The materiality math applies a pharmacy acquisition-cost gap (about the list-price level) to Lilly's net revenue. That is the wrong line, because U.S. revenue is net of about 59% GTN deductions (10-K p.54, p.49), so a lower-list SKU can carry far lower rebates and similar net. The same table also undercuts 'resetting the price paid.' The 7.5 mg single-dose pen NADAC rose from 510.44 (2024-02-21) to 526.00 (2026-09-23), and the KwikPen first appears 2026-05-20. So no existing SKU reset; a new cheaper SKU was added. Pen mix is undisclosed, so the $648M per 10% migration is unsupported. The claim that the KwikPen launched 'under the government deal' is not in any cited source. The press release p.1 says the deal has no commercial-channel pricing obligation.
verdicts.correction: At most: since May 2026 a lower-acquisition-cost Zepbound KwikPen SKU sits beside unchanged single-dose pens at retail. No revenue effect can be sized from NADAC because it is list-side, not net.

verdicts.argument: Zepbound is a material pick. H1 2026 Zepbound was $9,088M, or 21% of $42,773M (10-Q p.29, p.5), and Mounjaro plus Zepbound were 65% (10-Q p.26). The label facts check out. Zepbound covers weight management and OSA only (drug:zepbound p.2). Wegovy injection adds CV, age 12+ and MASH, and the tablets carry CV (drug:wegovy p.2). Foundayo is weight-only (p.2), 'with or without food' (p.4), with a 9 mg maximum alongside strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (p.6). The dollar consequence depends on post-2027 Medicare policy and an undisclosed Medicare share, so it cannot yet be sized (see c09).

overall: Every quoted figure is on its cited page and most single-line growth rates are computed correctly. However, several impact claims compare unlike things: two definitions of 'Other products' (c05), a consolidated liability against U.S. revenue (c04), pre-deal price erosion presented as the deal's concession (c01), and list-side NADAC applied to net revenue (c11). The candidates that survive at material scale are the 2025 inventory and receivable build (c03, now partly reversed for receivables), the 2025 GTN re-widening (~$1.2B), the tax step-up (~$0.94/share in 2025), and the contingent-consideration ceiling.
